key_insight: A large-scale, dynamic dataset captured from AAA games using a novel dual-screen stitched capture unlocks realistic, temporally coherent training data (4M frames, synchronized RGB + five G-buffer channels) to bridge the synthetic↔real domain gap for generative inverse and forward rendering.
problem_solved: Existing synthetic datasets lack the photorealism and temporal coherence needed to scale generative rendering methods to real-world scenarios, limiting model generalization and evaluation.
method: Curate a 4M-frame dynamic dataset from visually complex AAA games (720p / 30 FPS) spanning diverse scenes, effects, and environments.
Use a dual-screen stitched capture technique to record synchronized RGB and five G-buffer channels across continuous gameplay, preserving temporal continuity and rich rendering signals.
Provide this dataset as a benchmark for scaling and evaluating generative inverse and forward rendering models under realistic, temporally consistent conditions.
impact: Enables training and robust evaluation of generative renderers with far greater realism and temporal coherence, reducing the synthetic-to-real domain gap and accelerating progress in inverse/forward rendering research and applications.
visual_elements: Schematic diagram of the dual-screen stitched capture pipeline (how two screens are synchronized and stitched to produce RGB + G-buffers).
Before/after panel showing an RGB frame alongside its 5 G-buffer channels (e.g., normals, depth, albedo, roughness/specular, material ID) to illustrate the rich supervision.
Timeline or strip of consecutive frames demonstrating temporal continuity and motion coherence across captures.
Dataset summary card (big number: 4M frames, 720p@30FPS, list of scene/effect diversity) as an at-a-glance stat block.
paper_authors: Zheng-Hui Huang, Zhixiang Wang, Jiaming Tan, Ruihan Yu, Yidan Zhang
